provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-07-24T10 UTC: the Sun's centre is 0.54 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 2.62 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 95%, Earth in view 100%, both 95% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 211 Wh).
Longest darkness 16 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 489 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Darkest spell from 2029-08-05T03 UTC (16 h): terrain 8.9 km away blocks it (bearing 24 deg: skyline 1.51 deg, centre of the body at 1.20 deg).
Earth stays in view all mission: its closest pass, 2029-08-07T09 UTC, is 1.10 deg above the skyline (bearing 146 deg, set by the Moon's own curvature at -1.41 deg).

weak_battery.label: assumption: half the battery, e.g. a cell lost or a cold battery

words: Earth in view at touchdown, mid-mission and end: upload the plan at landing and confirm it on 2029-07-31.
1 dark spell, the longest 16 h; the battery lasts through every one, at best (sun-tracking panels).
With half the battery it dies at hour 288 (2029-08-05T10 UTC), even at best (sun-tracking panels).

checks: Sun and Earth positions: 124 checked against NASA JPL Horizons, all within 0.0003 deg.
Sunlight: matches NASA's PGDA map at the Shackleton rim, correlation 0.92 (2 m best fit).
cannot_see: Hazards smaller than the 20 m map, like the ~20 m crater IM-2 tipped into.
A tilted lander with fixed panels, like IM-1: survival here is an upper bound.

words: Land up to 93 h late and it is still safe on the exact point (no date here is safe if the lander misses by 100 m); even one lunation later (709 h) is safe.
Missed by up to 100 m: 2 of 17 points safe; at the point 50 m toward bearing 242 deg, its ground slopes 12.6 deg over 100 m.
